title: First nonzero projected D-delta-D boundary Taylor coefficient
question: For a local configuration Weyl character, what is the first exact generator coefficient created by adding a neighboring canonical Q3 bond, and does its force lie in the registered quartic energy weight?

model.derivation: delta_H(X)=i*[H,X]/hbar on the finite polynomial CCR core
model.weight_target: |partial_q B| <= C*(1+q^4+v^4)^(3/4) on the declared real configuration core

scope.not_closed: The result is an exact finite CCR-core Taylor coefficient and a conditional weighted force bound. It does not sum the time expansion or prove projected D, delta-D, exhaustion, group law, Hamiltonian-to-OS identification, common alpha, KMS/GNS, continuum, C6, Sector A or Pre-A closure.

adversarial_review.check: The derivation uses delta=i[H,.]/hbar, [B,p_x]=i*hbar*partial_q B, and W_a=exp(i*a*q_x/hbar); the hbar and sign are tracked.
The first generator difference is exactly zero because the bond is a q-multiplier; the force first appears at the second generator difference.
The cubic force is differentiated from the registered quadratic and Q3 edge bond, not imported as an abstract polynomial.
The W_Lambda^(3/4) bound is checked only on the declared real grid and is not promoted to an operator-domain theorem.
A second generator coefficient does not sum the real-time Duhamel series or control all spatial histories.
Lean R240 checks exact force coefficients, degree, and the hbar/chi fixture only.
No projected D, delta-D, OS/KMS, GNS gap, continuum, C6, Sector A or Pre-A closure follows.
No heat_root_incidence or canonical A1/R-192 production owner is supplied.
